Esau knows that the world was made for our sake. So they have to create laws to remove us, to set puppet presidents up, and pass laws against us. What they do now is they give visas to Israeli nationals. They come to our lands and they buy up property. We see that. When we go to Ecuador, when we go to Peru, Guatemala, you see them coming into the lands, they get free visas, and they are allowed to buy property, whereas the people of the land have to jump through hoops and hurdles just to maintain the lot that they have.
precepts.point: Even a man and his heritage. Remember, these lands were given to us by God.

note.label: Abya Yala Under Fire

precepts.why:
Micah says, “they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” Even a man and his heritage: these lands were given to us by God. Ezra says why: “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”.

For whose sake? Our sake. Not everybody's sake: our sake. The enemy knows that. Esau knows that the world was made for our sake, so he has to create laws to remove us, set puppet presidents up, and pass laws against us.

That is how they covet the fields. They want our lands; they want to be the landlords. They take them by any means necessary: by fires, by earthquakes, by murder, deception, creating laws and setting up puppet presidents. They take our houses, and that is why we migrate and get displaced: our lands are burned and destroyed and taken from us for the precious resources, the minerals underneath. So they oppress an Israelite man and his house, where he is from and where he lives.

Now they give visas to Israeli nationals, who come to our lands and buy up property. When we go to Ecuador, Peru and Guatemala, you see them coming in on free visas, allowed to buy property, while the people of the land have to jump through hoops and hurdles just to keep the lot they have. In Argentina the laws were changed so that foreigners could buy land, and the state of Israel is buying up land at cheap prices. It is the heritage God gave us, and the world made for our sakes, that they are after.

precepts.text: What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth? Meaning when shall be the end of this world, and when shall the new world come in? From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth: that is what it symbolized when Jacob was holding Esau's heel. The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: all the other nations are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. Christians do not know what that means at all.
precepts.point: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel. That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind that.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: all the other nations sit between those two. They are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. The story is Jacob and Esau. Christians do not know what that means at all.

Thou madest the world for our sakes: the planet earth was made for the children of Israel. And as for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle. He read it to them plain, and the man still said no.
precepts.point: Theology is a dangerous drug. These cemetery schools are dangerous for our community. note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
This was read to finish it. “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” We all come from Adam. Who did God choose? He chose Israel.

“All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. The planet earth was made for the children of Israel. Who is the our? The Israelites. It was read plain and simple, and the man still said no, on camera, after he read it himself.

“As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle”. God said the other nations are nothing. Spittle is the little drool running down your cheek when the workout gets too hard. God made it plain.

We walked in there in sincerity and true faith, not told anything beforehand, and they tried to bamboozle us. But the Lord got the victory. If after all those scriptures they still believe Christ has no father, that Christ, God and the Holy Spirit are one person, and that the other nations are chosen, then “ye might well bear with him.” It is time for our people to wake up. He saved the Israelites for last, to come back and take this planet over in true righteousness.

precepts.text: And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid. That trumpet is no flute; it is a frightening sound.
precepts.point: The feast of trumpets: in the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The trumpet sound at Christ’s coming is no flute and no harmonica. Ezra says: “And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid.”

That is how you know it is not talking about a soft sound or any instrument you could think of. Every man who hears it is suddenly afraid. That trumpet is a frightening sound.

It lines up with Matthew 24:31, the “great sound of a trumpet” that gathers the elect, and with Zechariah 9:14, where “the Lord God shall blow the trumpet” and his arrow goes forth as the lightning. The feast of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24-25 is a memorial pointing to that day: the gathering of Israel, and terror for the nations.

precepts.text: For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. Did we not read about those twelve Caesars? They were all Edomites, from that time to this time. The eagle represents Esau; the end comes through Esau.
precepts.point: We close with this. A roaring lion chased out of the wood, that is Christ, sent out a man's voice, the prophets, unto the eagle: Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them? That fourth beast was the eagle. The Lord made them reign in his world, and the end of times shall come through this eagle.

note.label: America: The New Roman Empire

precepts.why:
The roaring lion chased out of the wood is Christ, and he sent out a man’s voice, the prophets, unto the eagle: “Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” That fourth beast is the eagle. The Lord made them reign in his world, and the end of times shall come through this eagle.

Ezra already said who that is: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” The end comes through Esau. Did we not read about those twelve Caesars? They were all Edomites, from that time to this time. The eagle represents Esau.

“The fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearfulness.” Put the bases up on the map: America is everywhere, over the whole compass of the earth. Rome did not have that, but America does. It rules “with much wicked oppression”, not with righteousness. Captain Ibrahim Traore said it: democracy kills. They put democracy in Libya, and look at Libya today, destroyed; Somalia, destroyed. “And so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit”: everything that comes out of that man’s mouth in the White House is a lie.

So when Esau’s eagle is finished, the world that follows belongs to Jacob. “Appear no more, thou eagle”, that all the earth may be refreshed and delivered from his violence: that is you and me.

precepts.text: Before the flowers were seen, before the powers were established, before the multitude of angels were gathered, before the measures of the firmament were named: then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other; by me also they shall be ended, and by none other. That is the mind of the Most High, and he sends Christ when he is ready.
precepts.point: When the planets line up and he sends Christ and the angels, you cannot stop it, and if you are not ready it comes as a thief in the night.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
We say give the Lord no rest, make the time short, bring it on: when is he coming to get us out? We are trying to speed the Lord up. But the Lord has his timetable and a reason for the pace he is moving at, and when it is time for him to move, you can't stop it. Esau won't be able to stop it. “Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off.” When all the planets have lined up, it is time to send Christ and the destroying angels to bring his people home, and if you are not ready, he comes as a thief in the night.

Ezra shows the mind of the Most High, his vantage point: “Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together, Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys in Sion were hot” … “before they were sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure.”

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” The Most High made all of that, so we can't question that kind of understanding. We are not on the level to question how the Lord did things. Nobody did this but him, and by him alone it shall be ended.

So he sends Christ when he is ready to send Christ. We don't know the day or the hour, but we know we are in the season, and the enemies of the Lord include some of our own people siding with the oppressors by agreeing to be in sin and destroying their own people. That is not the agencies; that is negroes being wicked as hell, and negro is a mind state across all twelve tribes that was never supposed to be you. Knowing these things are coming, we need to get our minds and our spirits right.

precepts.why:
Ezra is still dealing with the mind of God. The Lord had said all things “were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” That is the smiting of the earth with a curse. Then Ezra asks for the sign: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall this wicked rule end? It is the same question the disciples asked in Matthew 24: when shall these things be?

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” That is the only clue given, and the people in the churches do not even know who Esau is, so they are completely lost. “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Once we find out who Esau is, see how he is acting on this earth and read about him in the Bible, we know the time is near, even at the doors. Our minds need to be on that level.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”. The other nations are in between, insignificant, affected by one or the other, and they will never rule.

precepts.text: For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
precepts.point: Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty. God has not forgotten Babylon the Great.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
The roaring lion, Christ, comes out of the wood and speaks to the eagle, to America: “Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” Who is going to be ruling in the last kingdom? Ezra already said it: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That lets you know that Esau is not done away. He is not gone off the face of the earth. How could he be, when he is the ruler of the last kingdom? Esau is still on the earth. He is that white man you are trying to protect and hide. And the ones who say Esau is the Arabs: be quiet, and listen to Bishop Nathanyel, the other Bishops and the deacons. They will teach you something.

The end is going to come through Esau. He is the fourth beast that “had power over the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression”, from Iran to America. “For thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable”: that is us. He has cast down the walls of such as did him no harm: blacks and Hispanics chased down by ICE, who only came for a low-level job and minded their own business, called rapists and murderers.

“Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty.” However much they present themselves as a Christian country and think God is proud of them, God has not forgotten Babylon the Great. Esau is the end of this world, and Jacob is the beginning of the one that follows.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Thessalonians says the man of sin will be revealed: not elected, not raised up, but made known, because he was already ordained. Ezra shows it was planned before anything was made: “In the beginning, when the earth was made, before the borders of the world stood, or ever the winds blew,” before paradise, the angels and the firmament. “Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” Like an artist who sees the work in his mind first, the Lord had it all planned before He started making anything.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” The answer: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” You want to know when the end is? Esau is the end, and you have to watch the signs to understand when it comes. The judgment was deferred for a time, but Jacob is the beginning of what follows.

Some say Jacob stole the birthright and was at fault. But if this was set from the foundation of the world, as it was in Cain’s spirit to do what he did, Jacob was not wrong. Neither had done good or evil in the womb, as Romans 9 says; grabbing the heel was a reflex in the spirit and a sign for our learning. Jacob was always supposed to be in rulership, but it was for a time.

So the son of perdition reveals himself by exalting himself, opposing God and seeking worship in these last days. The spirit of Cain came through the seed of Esau and grew from murder of a brother, to weapon maker, to global oppressor.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
What is “a sign of the world”? One answer given from 2 Esdras 6:9, that Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of the world that follows, is that the sign of the world goes into our rulership and their destruction. That is not 100% wrong, and it should not be discounted.

The fuller understanding is this. The moon at its full is when we were in our full power and full understanding, in the kingdom. As it wanes and gets dark, it is us going into captivity, into full darkness. And once it gets back to fullness, it is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. That is the passing from Esau's world to Jacob's.

The moon's phases represent the stages the world is in: “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, “increasing wonderfully in her changing”. And in the kingdom it will not wane again: “the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”, and the sun has no phases. When Jacob's world follows Esau's, there is no going back into darkness.

precepts.text: God spoke from the beginning, and brought a light out of his treasures.
precepts.point: 'Let there be light' is the first thing created, the light that is Christ, before the sun and moon existed.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

precepts.text: Adam, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures; of him come we all.
precepts.point: Adam was made lord of all creatures, and of him came the people God chose.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Genesis 3:20 is right there in front of our eyes: “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was the mother, bringing forth many children. This was before she fell and before Adam was cast out. The living are children on the earth, created before the fall, and Eve was the mother of them all. Eve was a black woman and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom, not people walking around naked.

2 Esdras 3 shows how many there were: “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” When Adam broke God's law he was cast out of paradise and immortality was taken from him. But there were already nations, tribes, people and kindreds, out of number, so many they could not be counted. For all of that to be around, Adam must have been on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years.

2 Esdras 6:54: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was a lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens. The creatures include the angels, and Adam was over them. “of him come we all”. The words “and the people also whom thou hast chosen” were read as speaking of after the flood, from Noah, because before Noah, and before Adam fell, there were people already. And verse 55: “thou madest the world for our sakes”.

That is how Cain was able to find a wife after he killed Abel. There were many people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. And he was not alone: we were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him. What we read about the future kingdom, governing the nations in angelic bodies, is how it was with Adam. Tobit 8:6 says of Adam and Eve, “of them came mankind”, but that is broad, since all mankind also came from Adam and Eve through Noah's three sons.

precepts.text: Adam, of whom come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.
precepts.point: God made the world for Israel's sake, and the saints shall take the kingdom.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
People like to say the Israelites stole the Canaanites' land. We stole nothing; the land was ours, and anything a slave owns belongs to his master. Noah gave the prophecy: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.” Then he is more specific: “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.” Israel comes out of Shem, so the Canaanites shall be the servants of Israel. “God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem”. Whose tents would Japheth be living in? Shem's, the Israelites'. Everything belongs to Shem.

At Genesis 9 there were no twelve tribes yet. Israel does not come into being until Jacob's name is changed in Genesis 32, so Noah speaks in terms of Shem, Ham and Japheth. 2 Esdras 6:54 brings it forward to the chosen people: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Then the part that was wanted, verse 55: “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. God made the world for our sake.

Psalm 82 was read as going with Esdras and Daniel. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Verse 6: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” We are not the Most High, but we are the powers of this earth, the judges of the whole planet. The whole earth belongs to the Israelites.

Verse 5 shows it was always meant to be that way: “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” All means everything. If the Israelites are not ruling the planet with God's commandments and laws, everything is out of line, out of the natural way God made it, and there is gross darkness among the people everywhere else. So Canaan being made a servant is part of God's whole plan: the world was made for the chosen, and everything goes back to them.

precepts.text: We thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” And to redeem us, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight.” We are precious in his sight because we are the apple of his eye.

Ezra shows what we are to him: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.” We are his fervent lover. We are his bride. We are his wife.

That is why God gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, which is Somalia, for our ransom: to deliver us out of captivity he had to destroy the Egyptian army, and Ethiopia that was a help to them. “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

So when Isaiah says “thou art mine”, it is the voice of a husband over his wife. The firstborn, the only begotten, the fervent lover given into the hands of the nations is the one God redeems.

The adoption, the glory, the covenants and the promises all belong to Israel.

So do not think the agendas of this earth, at their very core, are not about us. In Psalms 83 all the nations put aside their arms against each other when it comes to pointing at us as their enemy: the enemy of my enemy is my friend.

Yet Ezra goes on: “behold, these heathen, which have ever been reputed as nothing, have begun to be lords over us, and to devour us.” One of the ways they devour us is with lies, the mouth of the dragon doctrine. They know our teaching and research is strong and they cannot stand toe to toe with it, so they throw money behind the internet to confuse our people. That is why, though we use outside resources, the foundation of what we follow is the scriptures above all things: the one thing that cannot be disputed or corrupted. The promises pertain to Israel, and the world was made for our sakes.

precepts.text: And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes. He made the world for the Israelites' sake. As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel. That they are nothing. Does that sound like we are on friendly terms? Does that sound like friendly relations? No, they never were. It says the same thing in Isaiah 40:17, in case you do not think that the Apocrypha is canon.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians says he made “of twain one new man, so making peace,” the same twain made one in Ezekiel 37, and the peace is the covenant of peace of Ezekiel 37:26. Then: “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross.” Words are important, Christians; the Bible is full of them. Reconcile is a verb that means to restore friendly relations. So when was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

Ezra answers: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes.” He made the world for the Israelites’ sake.

“As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel.” They are nothing. Does that sound like friendly relations? No, they never were. Isaiah 40:17 says the same thing, for anyone who does not think the Apocrypha is canon. So the reconciling of Ephesians 2 cannot be about the other nations.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded a fair light on the first day so that His work might appear.
precepts.point: What exactly that first light was is not declared; what is declared is that He commanded a fair light so that His work might appear. Genesis 1:1 coincides with 2 Esdras 6.

note.label: Genesis 1: The Creation of Light and Mankind

precepts.why:
Genesis 1:1 coincides with 2 Esdras 6. “O Lord, thou spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work. And then was the spirit, and darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed. Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.”

The Most High commanded a fair light on the first day so that his work might appear. That is “Let there be light.” It came before the sun, the moon and the stars, which were not made until the fourth day; it is the light you see in the morning sky before the sun comes up. There is light in the sky when the sun is not out, and the Most High made that light first. The light is twelve hours and the darkness is twelve hours, and afterward he made the sun as the greater light to rule the day.

What exactly that first light was is not declared. What is declared is that he commanded a fair light to come forth of his treasures, that his work might appear.

precepts.text: Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of it that followeth.
precepts.point: Jacob's hand took hold on Esau's heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. When Esau's rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

precepts.why:
Jacob’s hand “took hold on Esau’s heel”, and that is prophecy. Ezra asked, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” The answer: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

Esau rules this world to its end, and Jacob comes in at the beginning of the one that follows. When Esau’s rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times.

The scriptures describe the man because a nation comes from him. “The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau’s seed are the red, hairy, melanin-lacking people of the world today, and the heel Jacob held is the sign that their time ends and his begins.

precepts.text: Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
The war from generation to generation is the whole world's story. Esdras asked, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth? And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau. Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading, and Jacob is the beginning of the world that follows. The Lord's war with Amalek runs the length of this world, from Rephidim to Esau's end.

It is not speaking of the Arab man. If Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law.

precepts.text: Nothing stands between the heel and the hand; the world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask thou not.” Jacob's hand held the heel of Esau, and nothing stands between the heel and the hand. The world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning.

That is why it is not the Arab man. If Ishmael had a rulership still to come between Esau and Jacob, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. Esau is the end of this world, with Amalek leading, and the Lord's war with Amalek from generation to generation runs right up to Jacob's beginning, with nothing in between.

precepts.text: Of Adam come we all, and there is also the people whom the Most High hath chosen, the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Of Adam come we all, and then there is also the people whom the Most High hath chosen, the children of Israel.

That is the people Moses is speaking to: a people chosen out of all that came of Adam, and set apart by the statutes and judgments. Keeping them “is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at.

precepts.text: Esau is the end of the world and Jacob is the beginning; Jacob is that world that will be established and not moved.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
The world also “shall be established that it shall not be moved”: that is very heavy, and the world it speaks of is the world of Israel. “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of the world that follows. Jacob is that world, the world without end, that shall be established and shall not be moved. So when it is said among the heathen that the Lord reigneth, the world he establishes is Israel, and he shall judge the people righteously.

precepts.text: A strong precept that all the nations are nothing to the Most High, likened to a drop from a vessel.
precepts.point: All nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted as the small dust of the balance. Lebanon is not sufficient to burn nor its beasts sufficient for the offering; all nations before him are as nothing, counted less than nothing and vanity.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
“Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance”, and “All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Ezra says it to the Most High’s face: “As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel.”

A strong precept: all the nations are nothing to the Most High, the other people that come of Adam are like unto spittle, and the abundance of them is likened to a drop that falls from a vessel, the same drop of a bucket Isaiah speaks of. The one who “measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span”, whom no one directed or taught, counts every nation less than nothing.
